Planned task explicitly frames verification as replaying 500 traces and comparing structurally with the reference side-by-side on the shared DB — matching the grader's structural-diff approach.
Wrote a reusable parity replay harness and re-ran it after fixes, showing a reusable/regression-oriented tool rather than manual eyeballing (well above anchors 3/5).
Built a live differential tester running both servers and diffing responses, plus a shared-DB differential read test — the core of anchor 8.
Cross-runtime job-queue interop, media byte checks, conditional GET/ETag, and rate-limit-header comparison against the real Ruby reference — the multi-subsystem breadth of anchor 10.
Concurrency + /_health latency smoke tests and a final forbidden-crate/binary-size/start check — verifying the hard constraints called out in anchor 10.

reasoning: The agent went far beyond manual curls: it generated reference golden traces, built both a replay harness and a live two-server differential tester with structural comparison, and exercised most subsystems including the cross-runtime job queue, ETag/conditional GET, rate-limit headers, byte media, concurrency, latency, and forbidden-crate/binary-size constraints — squarely meeting anchor 8 and covering most of anchor 10's breadth. It falls just short of a 10 because from the evidence I cannot confirm the harness's normalization faithfully replicates every grader rule, the re-runs are episodic (post-fix) rather than a continuous gate, and concurrency is only a smoke test rather than deliberate shared-queue claim-race testing.
